vocabulary.term: Convert Measurements within the Same System
vocabulary.termEs: Convertir medidas dentro del mismo sistema
vocabulary.definition: Rewriting a measurement in a different unit of the SAME system, such as feet into inches or liters into milliliters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Reescribir una medida en otra unidad del MISMO sistema, como pies a pulgadas o litros a mililitros.
vocabulary.cloze: Feet into inches stays inside the ___ measurement system.

examples.why: Both are customary units of capacity.
That crosses into the metric system.

vocabulary.definition: The ratio that links two units in the same measurement system, such as 12 inches to 1 foot. Within one system it is exact.
vocabulary.definitionEs: La razón que relaciona dos unidades del mismo sistema de medición, como 12 pulgadas a 1 pie. Dentro de un mismo sistema es exacta.
vocabulary.cloze: The ratio that trades one unit for another is a ___ ___.

examples.why: It is the fixed ratio that trades one unit for another.
That is the amount being converted, not the factor.

vocabulary.definition: A ratio that compares an amount to exactly 1 unit of another quantity, like 12 inches to 1 foot.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una razón que compara una cantidad con exactamente 1 unidad de otra cantidad, como 12 pulgadas por 1 pie.
vocabulary.visual: 12 : 1 — twelve inches for every one foot
vocabulary.cloze: A ratio comparing an amount to exactly ___ unit is a unit ratio.

examples.why: The second term is exactly one.
True, but not stated per one.

vocabulary.definition: To change a measurement from one unit to another without changing how much it is.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Cambiar una medida de una unidad a otra sin cambiar la cantidad que representa.
vocabulary.visual: 4 ft and 48 in are the same height, written two ways
vocabulary.cloze: To change a measurement to another unit without changing the amount is to ___.

examples.why: Same volume, smaller unit, bigger number.

vocabulary.definition: A family of units that go together — customary units like inches and feet, or metric units like milliliters and liters.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una familia de unidades que van juntas: unidades usuales como pulgadas y pies, o métricas como mililitros y litros.
vocabulary.visual: Customary: 12 in = 1 ft · Metric: 1,000 mL = 1 L
vocabulary.cloze: Inches and feet belong to the customary ___ ___; centimeters and meters to the metric one.

vocabulary.definition: Two number lines lined up so matching tick marks show two units for the same amount.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Dos rectas numéricas alineadas para que las marcas correspondientes muestren dos unidades de la misma cantidad.
vocabulary.cloze: Two lines whose matching ticks show the same amount in two units form a ___ ___ ___.

examples.text: Quarts on one line, cups on the other, aligned

vocabulary.definition: A table of equal ratios that lets you scale a conversion up or down one row at a time.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una tabla de razones iguales que permite escalar una conversión hacia arriba o hacia abajo fila por fila.
vocabulary.visual: 1 ft : 12 in, 2 ft : 24 in, 4 ft : 48 in

examples.why: Every column holds the same ratio.
The last column breaks the pattern.

vocabulary.cloze: A table whose every column holds the same comparison is a ___ ___.

revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Making Concrete
revealWordProblem.text:
Michael's mother needs to set four posts for her garden fence. She uses the concrete mix shown, and each post takes 250 ounces of mix.
Question: How many bags of concrete mix and how many quarts of water will she need?
revealWordProblem.imageAlt: A bag of fast-setting concrete with mixing directions: 1 bag (60 lbs) of concrete mix with 1 and one-half gallons of water.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: Four posts need 4 × 250 = 1,000 ounces of dry mix. Each 60-pound bag contains 60 × 16 = 960 ounces, so she must buy 2 bags. The directions use 1½ gallons = 6 quarts of water per full bag. If she mixes both full bags, she uses 12 quarts and has more concrete than the posts require. If she mixes only the needed 1,000 ounces, scale the water by the same ratio: (1,000 ÷ 960) × 6 = 6.25 quarts. State the assumption: buy 2 bags; use 6.25 quarts for the exact needed amount, or 12 quarts to mix both complete bags.

questions.stem: There are 12 inches in 1 foot. How many inches are in 5 feet?
questions.explanation: Inches are smaller than feet, so multiply by the unit ratio: 5 × 12 = 60 inches.
choiceFeedback: That subtracts 12 − 5. Converting is not a subtraction.
That adds 5 + 12. Converting scales the amount, so multiply.
hints: Write the unit ratio first: 12 inches : 1 foot.
Inches are smaller, so the number gets bigger — multiply.
questions.stemEs: Hay 12 pulgadas en 1 pie. ¿Cuántas pulgadas hay en 5 pies?
questions.explanationEs: Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies, así que multiplica por la razón unitaria: 5 × 12 = 60 pulgadas.
hintsEs: Escribe primero la razón unitaria: 12 pulgadas : 1 pie.
Las pulgadas son más pequeñas, así que el número se hace mayor — multiplica.

questions.stem: There are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter. How many milliliters are in 3 liters?
questions.explanation: Multiply by the unit ratio: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 milliliters.
choiceFeedback: 30 is far too small — one liter alone is already 1,000 mL.
hints: The unit ratio is 1,000 mL : 1 L.
Milliliters are smaller, so multiply.
questions.stemEs: Hay 1,000 mililitros en 1 litro. ¿Cuántos mililitros hay en 3 litros?
questions.explanationEs: Multiplica por la razón unitaria: 3 × 1,000 = 3,000 mililitros.
hintsEs: La razón unitaria es 1,000 mL : 1 L.
Los mililitros son más pequeños, así que multiplica.

questions.stem: There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. How many pounds is 48 ounces?
questions.explanation: Pounds are the LARGER unit, so divide: 48 ÷ 16 = 3 pounds.
choiceFeedback: That adds 48 + 16. Converting to a larger unit divides.
That multiplies. Multiplying goes to the smaller unit, not the larger one.
hints: Which unit is larger, an ounce or a pound?
Converting to the larger unit takes fewer of them, so divide.
questions.stemEs: Hay 16 onzas en 1 libra. ¿Cuántas libras son 48 onzas?
questions.explanationEs: Las libras son la unidad MÁS GRANDE, así que divide: 48 ÷ 16 = 3 libras.
hintsEs: ¿Cuál unidad es más grande, una onza o una libra?
Convertir a la unidad más grande requiere menos de ellas, así que divide.

steps: 1. Identify the conversion factor (e.g. 1 ft = 12 in, 1 km = 1,000 m)
2. Larger to smaller unit: Multiply by the conversion factor
3. Smaller to larger unit: Divide by the conversion factor
reviewHighlights.watchOut: A common mistake when converting within a measurement system is choosing the operation by habit instead of by unit size — multiplying every time. Converting 36 inches to feet by multiplying gives 36 × 12 = 432 feet, taller than a 40-story building. Ask first which unit is smaller: it takes MORE small units to make the same amount, so going to a smaller unit multiplies, and going to a larger unit divides.

level1.stem: How many inches are in 2 feet?
hints: Each foot is 12 inches. Find 2 × 12.
hintsEs: Cada pie mide 12 pulgadas. Halla 2 × 12.
level1.explanation: Write 1 foot and 12 inches in the table. Find the scale factor for the feet: 2 ÷ 1 = 2 Multiply by the same factor: 12 × 2 = 24
level1.explanationEs: Escribe 1 pie y 12 pulgadas en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de los pies: 2 ÷ 1 = 2 Multiplica por el mismo factor: 12 × 2 = 24

level1.stem: There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer. How many meters are in 6 kilometers?
level1.stemEs: Hay 1,000 metros en 1 kilómetro. ¿Cuántos metros hay en 6 kilómetros?
hints: Meters are smaller than kilometers, so multiply by 1,000.
hintsEs: Los metros son más pequeños que los kilómetros, así que multiplica por 1,000.
level1.explanation: Write 1 kilometer and 1,000 meters in the table. Find the scale factor for the kilometers: 6 ÷ 1 = 6 Multiply by the same factor: 1,000 × 6 = 6,000
level1.explanationEs: Escribe 1 kilómetro y 1,000 metros en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de los kilómetros: 6 ÷ 1 = 6 Multiplica por el mismo factor: 1,000 × 6 = 6,000

level1.stem: A rope is 5 yards long. There are 3 feet in 1 yard. How many feet long is the rope?
level1.stemEs: Una cuerda mide 5 yardas de largo. Hay 3 pies en 1 yarda. ¿Cuántos pies mide la cuerda?
hints: Feet are smaller than yards, so multiply: 5 × 3.
hintsEs: Los pies son más pequeños que las yardas, así que multiplica: 5 × 3.
level1.explanation: Write 1 yard and 3 feet in the table. Find the scale factor for the yards: 5 ÷ 1 = 5 Multiply by the same factor: 3 × 5 = 15
level1.explanationEs: Escribe 1 yarda y 3 pies en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de las yardas: 5 ÷ 1 = 5 Multiplica por el mismo factor: 3 × 5 = 15

level1.stem: How many inches are in 6 feet?
hints: Each foot is 12 inches. Inches are smaller, so multiply.
hintsEs: Cada pie mide 12 pulgadas. Las pulgadas son más pequeñas, así que multiplica.
level1.explanation: Write 1 foot and 12 inches in the table. Find the scale factor for the feet: 6 ÷ 1 = 6 Multiply by the same factor: 12 × 6 = 72 Check: smaller unit, so the number grows: 72 > 6
level1.explanationEs: Escribe 1 pie y 12 pulgadas en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de los pies: 6 ÷ 1 = 6 Multiplica por el mismo factor: 12 × 6 = 72 Comprueba: unidad más pequeña, así que el número crece: 72 > 6

level1.stem: There are 16 ounces in 1 pound. How many ounces are in 5 pounds?
level1.stemEs: Hay 16 onzas en 1 libra. ¿Cuántas onzas hay en 5 libras?
hints: Ounces are smaller than pounds. Will you get more or fewer ounces?
hintsEs: Las onzas son más pequeñas que las libras. ¿Tendrás más o menos onzas?
level1.explanation: Write 1 pound and 16 ounces in the table. Find the scale factor for the pounds: 5 ÷ 1 = 5 Multiply by the same factor: 16 × 5 = 80 Check: smaller unit, so the number grows: 80 > 5
level1.explanationEs: Escribe 1 libra y 16 onzas en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de las libras: 5 ÷ 1 = 5 Multiplica por el mismo factor: 16 × 5 = 80 Comprueba: unidad más pequeña, así que el número crece: 80 > 5

level2.stem: Leo says 24 inches is 288 feet, because 24 × 12 = 288. Is he right? How many feet is 24 inches?
level2.stemEs: Leo dice que 24 pulgadas son 288 pies, porque 24 × 12 = 288. ¿Tiene razón? ¿Cuántos pies son 24 pulgadas?
hints: Feet are larger than inches. Should there be more feet or fewer feet?
hintsEs: Los pies son más grandes que las pulgadas. ¿Debe haber más pies o menos pies?
level2.explanation: Write 12 inches and 1 foot in the table. Find the scale factor for the inches: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 Multiply the feet by the same factor: 1 × 2 = 2 Check: feet are larger, so fewer feet: 2 < 24
level2.explanationEs: Escribe 12 pulgadas y 1 pie en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de las pulgadas: 24 ÷ 12 = 2 Multiplica los pies por el mismo factor: 1 × 2 = 2 Comprueba: los pies son más grandes, así que hay menos pies: 2 < 24

level2.stem: A plank is 51 inches long. How many feet long is it? Write your answer as a decimal.
level2.stemEs: Una tabla mide 51 pulgadas de largo. ¿Cuántos pies mide? Escribe tu respuesta como decimal.
hints: Feet are larger than inches, so divide by 12.
hintsEs: Los pies son más grandes que las pulgadas, así que divide entre 12.
level2.explanation: Write 12 inches and 1 foot in the table. Find the scale factor for the inches: 51 ÷ 12 = 4.25 Multiply 1 by the same factor: 1 × 4.25 = 4.25 Check with multiplication: 4.25 × 12 = 51
level2.explanationEs: Escribe 12 pulgadas y 1 pie en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de las pulgadas: 51 ÷ 12 = 4.25 Multiplica 1 por el mismo factor: 1 × 4.25 = 4.25 Comprueba con una multiplicación: 4.25 × 12 = 51

level2.stem: How many inches are in 8 feet?
hints: Inches are smaller than feet. Multiply by 12.
hintsEs: Las pulgadas son más pequeñas que los pies. Multiplica por 12.
level2.explanation: Write 1 foot and 12 inches in the table. Find the scale factor for the feet: 8 ÷ 1 = 8 Multiply by the same factor: 12 × 8 = 96 Check: smaller unit, so the number grows: 96 > 8
level2.explanationEs: Escribe 1 pie y 12 pulgadas en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de los pies: 8 ÷ 1 = 8 Multiplica por el mismo factor: 12 × 8 = 96 Comprueba: unidad más pequeña, así que el número crece: 96 > 8

level2.stem: Bag A of rice weighs 2 pounds. Bag B weighs 30 ounces. How many more ounces does the heavier bag weigh?
level2.stemEs: La bolsa A de arroz pesa 2 libras. La bolsa B pesa 30 onzas. ¿Cuántas onzas más pesa la bolsa más pesada?
hints: Write both weights in ounces before you compare. There are 16 ounces in 1 pound.
hintsEs: Escribe los dos pesos en onzas antes de comparar. Hay 16 onzas en 1 libra.
level2.explanation: Write 1 pound and 16 ounces in the table. Find the scale factor for the pounds: 2 ÷ 1 = 2 Multiply the ounces by the same factor: 16 × 2 = 32 Subtract the two weights: 32 − 30 = 2
level2.explanationEs: Escribe 1 libra y 16 onzas en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de las libras: 2 ÷ 1 = 2 Multiplica las onzas por el mismo factor: 16 × 2 = 32 Resta los dos pesos: 32 − 30 = 2

level2.stem: A pitcher holds 2 quarts of juice. There are 4 cups in 1 quart. How many cups of juice does the pitcher hold?
level2.stemEs: Una jarra contiene 2 cuartos de galón de jugo. Hay 4 tazas en 1 cuarto de galón. ¿Cuántas tazas de jugo contiene la jarra?
hints: Cups are smaller than quarts, so you will get more cups.
hintsEs: Las tazas son más pequeñas que los cuartos de galón, así que tendrás más tazas.
level2.explanation: Write 1 quart and 4 cups in the table. Find the scale factor for the quarts: 2 ÷ 1 = 2 Multiply by the same factor: 4 × 2 = 8 Check: smaller unit, so the number grows: 8 > 2
level2.explanationEs: Escribe 1 cuarto de galón y 4 tazas en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de los cuartos de galón: 2 ÷ 1 = 2 Multiplica por el mismo factor: 4 × 2 = 8 Comprueba: unidad más pequeña, así que el número crece: 8 > 2

level3.stem: A rope measures 7 feet. Using 1 foot = 12 inches, how long is the rope in inches?
choiceFeedback: That divides 7 by 12, converting the wrong direction. Inches are smaller than feet, so the count gets bigger.
That leaves the measurement in feet. Each foot holds 12 inches, so multiply.
That adds 7 and 12. Converting to a smaller unit multiplies: 7 x 12.

level3.stem: Ana says 2 feet 6 inches is 2.6 feet. What is the correct length in feet, as a decimal?
level3.stemEs: Ana dice que 2 pies 6 pulgadas son 2.6 pies. ¿Cuál es la longitud correcta en pies, como decimal?
hints: How many inches are in 1 foot? What part of a foot is 6 inches?
hintsEs: ¿Cuántas pulgadas hay en 1 pie? ¿Qué parte de un pie son 6 pulgadas?
level3.explanation: Write 12 inches and 1 foot in the table. Find the scale factor from 12 to 6: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 Divide the feet by the same factor: 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 Add the whole feet: 2 + 0.5 = 2.5
level3.explanationEs: Escribe 12 pulgadas y 1 pie en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de 12 a 6: 12 ÷ 6 = 2 Divide los pies entre el mismo factor: 1 ÷ 2 = 0.5 Suma los pies enteros: 2 + 0.5 = 2.5

level3.stem: A table is 66 inches long. How many feet long is it? Write your answer as a decimal.
level3.stemEs: Una mesa mide 66 pulgadas de largo. ¿Cuántos pies mide? Escribe tu respuesta como decimal.
hints: Feet are larger than inches. Divide by 12.
hintsEs: Los pies son más grandes que las pulgadas. Divide entre 12.
level3.explanation: Write 12 inches and 1 foot in the table. Find the scale factor for the inches: 66 ÷ 12 = 5.5 Multiply 1 by the same factor: 1 × 5.5 = 5.5 Check with multiplication: 5.5 × 12 = 66
level3.explanationEs: Escribe 12 pulgadas y 1 pie en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de las pulgadas: 66 ÷ 12 = 5.5 Multiplica 1 por el mismo factor: 1 × 5.5 = 5.5 Comprueba con una multiplicación: 5.5 × 12 = 66

level3.stem: A carton holds 2,250 milliliters of juice. How many liters of juice is that?
level3.stemEs: Un cartón contiene 2,250 mililitros de jugo. ¿Cuántos litros de jugo son?
hints: Liters are larger than milliliters. There are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter.
hintsEs: Los litros son más grandes que los mililitros. Hay 1,000 mililitros en 1 litro.
level3.explanation: Write 1,000 milliliters and 1 liter in the table. Find the scale factor for the milliliters: 2,250 ÷ 1,000 = 2.25 Multiply 1 by the same factor: 1 × 2.25 = 2.25 Check with multiplication: 2.25 × 1,000 = 2,250
level3.explanationEs: Escribe 1,000 mililitros y 1 litro en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de los mililitros: 2,250 ÷ 1,000 = 2.25 Multiplica 1 por el mismo factor: 1 × 2.25 = 2.25 Comprueba con una multiplicación: 2.25 × 1,000 = 2,250

level3.stem: A track is 400 meters around. How many laps does a runner need to run 3 kilometers?
level3.stemEs: Una pista mide 400 metros por vuelta. ¿Cuántas vueltas necesita un corredor para correr 3 kilómetros?
hints: Write both distances in meters first.
hintsEs: Primero escribe las dos distancias en metros.
level3.explanation: Write 1 kilometer and 1,000 meters in the table. Find the scale factor for the kilometers: 3 ÷ 1 = 3 Multiply the meters by the same factor: 1,000 × 3 = 3,000 Divide by the length of one lap: 3,000 ÷ 400 = 7.5
level3.explanationEs: Escribe 1 kilómetro y 1,000 metros en la tabla. Halla el factor de escala de los kilómetros: 3 ÷ 1 = 3 Multiplica los metros por el mismo factor: 1,000 × 3 = 3,000 Divide entre la longitud de una vuelta: 3,000 ÷ 400 = 7.5

predict.stem: Before you build the table — there are 12 inches in 1 foot. How many feet is 60 inches?
predict.explanation: Feet are larger than inches, so there will be FEWER of them: 60 ÷ 12 = 5 feet.
choiceFeedback: That multiplies by 12 out of habit. Going to a LARGER unit gives a smaller number, so divide.
That adds 12 instead of dividing by it.
That subtracts 12. The conversion multiplies or divides, never adds or subtracts.

steps.title: Find how many bags
steps.say: One bag is not quite enough, so she buys 2.

workedSteps.answer: Buy 2 bags. Use 6.25 quarts of water for exactly the 1,000 ounces needed, or 12 quarts to mix both full bags.
